answer.evidence: I found no compact patch that would mark a planted artifact. The units with clearly trained structure fall into two groups. (1) Centre-blob units have broad positive weights over the central field, with values up to 90-99: unit 8 (rows ~5-21, cols ~4-18), unit 18 (rows ~7-17, cols ~8-17), unit 20 (rows ~6-18, cols ~6-16) and unit 29 (rows ~6-18, cols ~5-17). Unit 2 is broadly positive everywhere. Tracing W2 then W3 gives net positive (malignant) contributions for units 8, 18 and 20, with unit 18 the strongest; unit 29 is roughly neutral. (2) Surround/ring units have positive weights along the image periphery and negative weights in the centre (down to -90s): unit 17, unit 23 (strongest on rows 0-3 but also column 0, column 23 and row 23) and unit 27. Units 17 and 23 trace to a net benign push, which fits 'dark centre, bright surroundings = small nodule'. Unit 27 traces mildly positive, so the ring units are not one-directional. The remaining units look like near-initialisation noise (|w| mostly under ~75, no spatial structure). No unit has a small, isolated cluster of large weights in a corner or edge, and no localized high-gain pathway feeds the output. Moderate residual uncertainty remains because the top-row emphasis in unit 23 could hide a weak edge artifact, but it is part of a full-border pattern rather than a discrete marker.
answer.main_feature: The model mainly scores the amount and extent of bright (dense) tissue in the central region where the nodule sits: large, solid central opacity pushes toward malignant. A dark centre with only peripheral brightness, i.e. a small nodule, pushes toward benign.
